solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Responsible for actors' melancholy

parts.note: to be over something is to be in charge of it, responsible for it
the actors in a production together form its cast

explanation.surface: A director is blamed for the gloomy mood of the theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melancholy' looks like the actors' state of mind, but it is the definition, in the sense of a dull, gloomy sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dull and gloomy, and figuratively a mood can be equally sombre or melancholy.

clue.text: Waste unknown amount in Irish county

parts.note: offal is animal waste, the trimmings left after butchering
in algebra Y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone spends an unknown sum on rubbish somewhere in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFALY is a county in the Irish midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Offaly is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in the province of Leinster.

clue.text: One worried about onset of dotage is an inventor

indicators.note: worried here means pulled about and tugged out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the onset of something is its beginning, so only the first letter of dotage is taken

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about growing senile turns out to be a creative genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges ONE, D (the onset of 'dotage') and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, the American behind the phonograph and a practical light bulb, is a famous example of an inventor.

clue.text: Trim model comes up to expectations

parts.note: to trim hair or a hedge is to cut it
to model for an artist is to sit for them

explanation.surface: A neat little fashion model lives up to what was hoped of her.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'cuts it' means is good enough, meeting the required standard.

clue.text: Lacking money for a biscuit

parts.note: to be short of something is to lack it
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone without cash can only afford a cheap biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORTBREAD is a rich, crumbly Scottish butter biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a crumbly butter biscuit, the kind of item called a cookie in America.

clue.text: Up to date intelligence prior to strike

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: wit is quick intelligence
to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: Current intelligence reports arriving just before an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'with it' is an informal idiom for being fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: Raise in fold

parts.note: a crease is a fold in paper or cloth

explanation.surface: Lift something up inside a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a price or amount is to increase it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Clearance given by boss on range

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another means placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the head of an organisation is its boss
room is scope or range, as in room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Permission granted by the manager for use of the shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearance' suggests an official permission, but it is the space above a vehicle or under a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the vertical clearance available, such as the space between a vehicle's roof and a bridge.

clue.text: Trying more ties out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Testing even more neckties is getting exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trying wears on your patience, so it is tiresome, a direct synonym in the adjective sense.

clue.text: False story about king results in conflict

indicators.note: about means going round, so the story wraps the king's letter

parts.note: fiction is an invented, untrue story
R, from Latin rex, is the standard abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A lie told about a monarch sparks a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is disagreement or tension between people, a near synonym for conflict.

clue.text: Cake, girl putting last in mouth

indicators.note: the mouth is the opening, so the final letter is moved to the front of the name

parts.note: Claire is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl puts the last bit of cake in her mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting last in mouth' moves the E at the end of CLAIRE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry cake filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Try to discover the facts about family in play, first from Orton

definitions.text: Try to discover the facts about

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Loot is a black comedy by the playwright Joe Orton
kin are one's family

indicators.note: first from means only the initial letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Researching the family depicted in an Orton play.
explanation.walkthrough: Orton's own play LOOT is the container, so the reference to Orton does double duty in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into a matter is to investigate it, trying to establish the facts about it.

clue.text: Refuse new bride bit of sex

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of bride are rearranged
a bit of the word means just its first letter here

explanation.surface: A newlywed turns down any suggestion of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish. 'new' rearranges BRIDE to DEBRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or waste, the noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: Manoeuvre Roller into short passage

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Steer the Rolls-Royce into a narrow alley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritornello is a short recurring instrumental passage in music, especially in baroque concertos.

clue.text: Sudden inspiration in squall by leader in boat

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other
the leader in a word is its first letter

parts.note: a squall is a sudden storm, typically with rain

explanation.surface: A bright idea comes to the captain of a boat caught in a squall.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a sudden clever idea, chiefly in British usage, also called a brainwave.

clue.text: Product of a man with oils?

definitions.text: Product of a man with oils?

indicators.note: a product is something made, so the letters of the words are remade into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a painter made using oil paints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Product of' rearranges A MAN and OILS; the whole clue also describes Leonardo's oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's portrait, painted in oils by a man.

clue.text: Knife fight involving upset drunk

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the fight wraps the other piece

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or argument

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk upset in a scuffle produces a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the slang word for drunk upside down, and 'involving' places it inside the hyphenated word for a scrap; 'Knife fight' looks like one phrase but splits after 'Knife'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim dagger with a narrow tapering blade.

clue.text: Mark in genuine denial

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: genuine means real
a mark is a target, as is a butt, the object of ridicule or aim

explanation.surface: A sign of authenticity in a sincere refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction of a claim, a formal denial of it.

clue.text: Not drinking what one mixed? No good, upon reflection

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so these letters are rearranged
a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what a cocktail would have been, then deciding against it after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges WHAT ONE into ONTHEWA, and 'upon reflection' turns NO G into GON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'on the wagon' is an idiom for abstaining from alcohol.

clue.text: Superb western chamois

parts.note: the izard is the chamois of the Pyrenees

explanation.surface: Praising a splendid mountain goat from the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wizard' as an adjective is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizard is old-fashioned British slang meaning excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Acquire gold carriage

parts.note: to land a job or prize is to acquire it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Buying a gilded coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.

clue.text: Search for a variety of polecat

definitions.meaning: to ... about or ... out is to search persistently
the domesticated albino form of the polecat, kept for hunting rabbits

explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a tame polecat, and its burrowing habit gives the verb meaning to rummage or search.

clue.text: Using one's maximum powers may get everyone on strike

parts.note: all means everyone
workers who are out are on strike

explanation.surface: A full walkout may result when every worker downs tools.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out effort uses every ounce of strength, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Close friend's secret

definitions.meaning: a very close companion or confidant
private or personal, as of thoughts or details

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a confidant; as an adjective it means private and personal.

clue.text: Completely at home, small child given love

parts.note: in means at home
a tot is a small child
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Fully content at home with an adored toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase 'in toto' means in its entirety, wholly.

clue.text: Circle newspaper article about northern shrub

parts.note: a circle has the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article wraps the other letter

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial about a northern bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen Mediterranean shrub with poisonous leaves and showy flowers.

clue.text: A count attached to old American space programme

parts.note: a poll is a count of votes or heads

explanation.surface: A tally linked to some former American space effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was NASA's lunar programme that landed astronauts on the Moon between 1969 and 1972.

clue.text: Leave with desire to throttle theologian for something much sought-after

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: to throttle is to grip round the throat, so desire surrounds the theologian

parts.note: lust is strong desire
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Walk away rather than let craving strangle a scholar of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as 'gold dust' is rare and highly prized, so it is much sought-after.
